name: Diurán
text: Diurán, sometimes called Diurán the Rhymer, was a poet of early Ireland. He sailed as a companion of Máel Dúin on the fabulous voyage known as Imram Curaig Máele Dúin. His adventures aboard included a plunge into a magic fountain. The plunge gave him lifelong youth and good health. He also cut free the crew by severing a stranger's arm. The stranger had held them fast with a magical thread. He tore a piece of net from a silver pillar and laid it on the altar at Armagh. Most scholars treat that final offering as a later Christian touch added to the older voyage text.

okr.objective: Diurán the Rhymer as the poet who sailed with Máel Dúin on the immram voyage.
